jobs.description:
Company Description
The National Veterans Foundation (NVF) is dedicated to serving the crisis management, information, and referral needs of U.S. veterans and their families. NVF operates the nation’s only 24/7 toll-free helpline for veterans and their families and runs public awareness programs that highlight the ongoing needs of America’s veterans. The organization provides outreach services that connect veterans and families with food, clothing, transportation, employment, and other essential resources. Staffed by trained veterans and licensed volunteer counselors, NVF has assisted more than 400,000 veterans with medical treatment, substance abuse and PTSD counseling, VA benefits advocacy, food, shelter, employment training, legal aid, and suicide intervention. Recognized for its expertise in Post Traumatic Stress Disorder and continuous innovation in services, NVF remains committed to supporting all who seek emotional support and assistance.
Role Description
The Chief Development Officer (CDO) is a full-time, hybid role based in Los Angeles, CA, responsible for leading and expanding all fundraising and development activities for the National Veterans Foundation. The CDO will design and execute comprehensive development strategies, including individual giving, major gifts, planned giving, annual campaigns, corporate and foundation support, and special events. Day-to-day responsibilities include setting revenue goals, managing development budgets, overseeing donor cultivation and stewardship, and preparing compelling proposals, reports, and fundraising communications. This role will collaborate closely with the Founder, Executive Director, Board of Directors, and program staff to align fundraising efforts with organizational priorities and mission impact. The CDO will also build and mentor a development team, implement systems to track donor engagement, and represent NVF at community events, meetings, and presentations to strengthen relationships with supporters and partners.
Qualifications

Demonstrated expertise in philanthropy and fundraising, including Planned Giving and Annual Giving, with a track record of meeting or exceeding revenue goals.
Strong strategic planning and budgeting skills, with experience developing and managing multi-year development plans and departmental budgets.
Experience building and maintaining relationships with individual donors, foundations, corporations, and community partners, including major gift cultivation and stewardship.
Proficiency in using donor management systems, data analysis, and reporting to support evidence-based fundraising decisions.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to craft persuasive proposals, cases for support, and donor correspondence.
Leadership experience managing and mentoring staff or volunteers in a development or nonprofit environment.

jobs.title: Deputy Director, Thurgood Marshall Institute
jobs.description:
The NAACP Legal Defense & Educational Fund, Inc. (LDF) is the country’s first and foremost civil and human rights law organization. Founded in 1940 under the leadership of Thurgood Marshall, who subsequently became the first Black U.S. Supreme Court Justice, LDF was launched at a time when the nation’s aspirations for equality and due process of law were stifled by widespread state-sponsored racial inequality. From that era to the present, LDF’s mission has been transformative — to achieve racial justice, equality, and an inclusive society.

LDF’s litigation, public policy advocacy, and public education programs in the substantive areas of criminal justice, economic justice, education, and political participation seek to ensure the fundamental and basic human rights of all people to quality education, economic opportunity, the right to vote and fully participate in democracy, and the right to a fair and just judicial system. LDF continues to make an impact in the area of public service and was recognized by Fast Company as one of its 2023 Brands That Matter under its public service category.

The Thurgood Marshall Institute

Since its founding under the leadership of Thurgood Marshall in 1940, LDF has been committed to transforming this nation’s promise of equality into reality for all Americans. In 2015, LDF celebrated its 75th anniversary with the launch of the Thurgood Marshall Institute (TMI). The Institute is a collaborative research and archival hub within LDF that combines a multidisciplinary approach to advocacy with LDF’s traditional litigation strengths to advance a modern vision of racial justice. The Institute’s goals are to enhance LDF’s use and mobilization of research, archives, and public education to increase its capacity to fight for racial equity, justice, and a more inclusive democracy through targeted advocacy and high-impact communications campaigns.

Through TMI, LDF generates and integrates innovative research, advocacy, archival materials, and strategic communications aimed at educating the public and key decision-makers. This added capacity leverages LDF’s litigation expertise, advocacy experience, and unique leadership role on matters of race, law, and policy to shape the narrative on racial justice and equity. Through targeted campaigns that attack entrenched problems of racial bias, TMI advances holistic strategies to achieve obtainable and lasting solutions on issues of criminal justice, political participation, education, and economic opportunity. In addition, the Institute serves as an active convener of thought-leaders from various disciplines to engage on cutting-edge issues of racial justice in both public and private fora.

In 2024, TMI launched LDF Recollection: A Civil Rights Legal Archive . The website contains stories and primary source materials documenting the history of LDF and the Civil Rights Movement in the U.S. This initiative represents a significant milestone in LDF’s mission to preserve and promote our legacy of civil rights, activism, and advocacy. The core of the website is a searchable digital collection with over 12,000 legal documents, letters, photographs, press releases, original oral history interviews, and other materials from the LDF Archives. The archivists’ work is ongoing as they actively survey, arrange, describe, and digitize select records from LDF’s collection of over 8,000 boxes and multiple terabytes of born-digital records. Their workflow also includes a final step in which the team’s Archives Counsel reviews digitized documents to ensure they do not contain privileged, confidential, or sensitive information.

LDF operates in a hybrid work environment where employees are expected to be in the office a minimum of two days per week, unless otherwise indicated.

Along with a resume and cover letter, applicants are expected to submit an independently authored piece of writing. While it may have undergone review or editing by others, it should primarily reflect your own work.

Responsibilities

Departmental Leadership

Reports directly to the TMI Director and provides supervision across both the Research and Archives teams.
Serve as a thought-partner with the TMI Director to develop and implement strategic goals for the department, ensuring alignment with broader organizational objectives.
Lead department meetings and retreats, including agenda development in collaboration with the TMI Director and Managers, to ensure strategic alignment and team engagement.
Collaborate with TMI Director on budgeting and the recruitment and hiring of key Research and Archives staff, including TMI fellows and scholars, to ensure alignment with organizational and departmental needs and strategic priorities.
Guide and mentor staff to fully understand and effectively execute their job responsibilities, fostering accountability through performance reviews, professional development, and leadership opportunities.
Build and maintain relationships with internal and external stakeholders to enhance departmental initiatives and resources, which include managing budgets, grant compliance, and vendor contracts in coordination with the TMI Director.
Develop and complete annual professional development plans to stay current on developments in the field.
Represents TMI in public forums, including conferences, media appearances, and other external engagements, to elevate the Institute’s research, archival projects, and advocacy.
Help identify and support cross-functional projects that connect research, archives, and public education.

Archives Oversight

Lead in coordination with the TMI Director the strategy, development, and execution of archival projects to preserve and promote LDF’s civil rights legacy in collaboration with the team.
Work with the Archives Department on refinement, implementation, and management of LDF’s efforts to review its archived records for publication.
Work with the Archives Department on the dissemination and promotion of LDF’s archival records, including those housed at the Library of Congress, both internally and externally.
Support archives team members through meetings to ensure work product meets high-quality standards, maintains TMI’s voice, and advances LDF advocacy goals within an established timeframe and budget.

Research Oversight

Develop and support the implementation of the research agenda to align with TMI and LDF’s strategic priorities, including qualitative and quantitative research design, public-facing reports, and policy briefs in collaboration with TMI Director.
Supervise research team members, including senior researchers, fellows, and associated team members, to ensure products meet high-quality research standards, maintain TMI’s voice, advance LDF advocacy goals, and are completed within an established timeframe and budget.
Support TMI researchers in the preparation and submission of IRB applications, grant submissions, and the submission of grant reports of research activities.
Review research findings for publication, ensuring that reports, papers, and presentations accurately reflect the data and adhere to ethical standards across all research stages, from proposal to publication, to prevent misconduct and promote transparency.
Coordinate the evaluation of TMI’s publications for external review in collaboration with the TMI Director to ensure the integrity and quality of research outputs. Selecting appropriate reviewers, facilitating constructive dialogue, and synthesizing insights guide revisions or project advancements, maintaining scholarly excellence and innovation.
Supervise the oversight of the Social Science Research Network (SSRN), National Police Funding Database, and the Death Row USA Report, ensuring the reports and website data are current.
Develop and update research policies and procedures (manual).
Oversee interdepartmental rapid research requests, ensuring that requests are aligned with LDF’s strategic priorities.
Provide editorial oversight and strategic review of TMI’s research publications to ensure rigor, clarity, and alignment with LDF’s advocacy goals.
Facilitate interdisciplinary collaborations with scholars and advocacy partners.

Qualifications

Ph.D. required, J.D. and/or MLIS equivalent preferred, advanced terminal degree in a relevant field (e.g., law, criminal justice, sociology, education policy, public health, political science, demography, or other social science field).
Minimum of 10 years of professional experience with expertise in civil rights history, academic research, or civil rights advocacy, including supervisory experience.
Experience developing research on civil rights issues with a focus on addressing racial discrimination and/or racially disparate outcomes.
A minimum of 8 years of experience managing staff, including nonprofit program management, with a demonstrated ability to lead diverse teams.
Strong written and oral communication skills, with a strong track record of published work in academic (peer-reviewed or law review), policy, or public-facing outlets.
Deep knowledge of Black history, civil rights history, and contemporary racial justice issues.
Significant experience working within nonprofit or academic institutions.
Proven success managing diverse, multidisciplinary teams across program areas.
Adaptable, collaborative, self-motivated, creative problem solver with careful attention to detail.
Experience with public speaking with the ability to effectively represent LDF’s mission to diverse external audiences.
Experience developing and managing publications, research workflows, and strategic campaigns required.

Preferred

Demonstrated expertise in archival management, collections development, and historical research.
Experience managing budgets.
Successful record of using multiple campaign strategies to achieve positive social change, including, for example, advocacy, research, archives, organizing, communications, and litigation.
Familiarity with open-access publication platforms, data visualization tools, or digital humanities methods is a plus.

The Foundation

The John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation
is one of the nation's largest independent philanthropic foundations, dedicated to building a more just, verdant, and peaceful world. Established in 1978 through the legacy of John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur, the Foundation supports creative people, effective institutions, and influential networks that are advancing solutions to some of the world's most pressing social and environmental challenges.

Through programmatic grantmaking, impact investing, strategic partnerships, convening power, and collaborations at scale, MacArthur strives toward transformative change on some of the world’s most pressing social issues, including the existential threats of climate change
, criminal justice reform
, revitalizing local news
in the United States, expanding who creates, uses, and benefits from artificial intelligence
, strengthening Native communities
, and empowering young people in Nigeria
.

In addition to their award programs, MacArthur Fellows
, and 100&Change
, the Foundation continues its historic commitments to the role of journalism
in a responsible and responsive democracy and to the strength and vitality of their headquarters city, Chicago
. The Foundation also works to strengthen ecosystems of people, organizations and networks working on deploying catalytic capital
,
strengthening the philanthropic sector
and addressing the social impacts of technology
.

Across its portfolio, the Foundation approaches its work with urgency, intellectual rigor, adaptability, and a commitment to continuous learning, leveraging grants, impact investments, communications, convenings, contracts, and partnerships to achieve measurable and lasting impact.

Since its founding, MacArthur has awarded more than $9.19 billion through grants and impact investments
to approximately 11,000 organizations and individuals and has supported work in 119 countries. Headquartered in Chicago, the Foundation maintains offices in India and Nigeria. As of December 31, 2025, MacArthur's assets totaled approximately $9.9 billion. In 2025 alone, the Foundation provided approximately $561.6 million in grants and program-related investments and committed an estimated $647 million in charitable spending, reflecting its continued commitment to investing boldly in solutions that create meaningful and enduring change.

The Opportunity

The MacArthur Foundation seeks an accomplished, strategic, and values-driven executive to serve as its next Managing Director, People & Culture. Reporting directly to the Foundation’s President and serving as a member of the Foundation's executive leadership team, the Managing Director will provide vision, strategy, and leadership for all aspects of the Foundation's people and culture agenda. This executive will play a critical role in ensuring that MacArthur continues to attract, develop, engage, support, and retain exceptional talent while cultivating a workplace culture that enables staff to thrive and advance the Foundation's mission.

As a trusted advisor to the President and senior leadership team, the Managing Director will serve as the Foundation's chief people strategist, leading efforts that strengthen organizational effectiveness, leadership capacity, employee engagement, and long-term talent sustainability. The successful candidate will combine strategic perspective with operational excellence, helping to shape the employee experience while ensuring that people practices, programs, and policies align with MacArthur's mission, values, and commitment to the Just Imperative.

MacArthur is navigating a period of change and heightened ambition. As the Foundation responds to an increasingly complex external environment, embraces new technologies, and seeks to deliver greater impact without proportionate growth in its workforce, the Managing Director will help shape how the organization works, leads, collaborates, and adapts. This leader will help MacArthur sustain the best of its highly collaborative, intellectually curious, and mission-driven culture while strengthening organizational agility, accountability, clarity, and effectiveness.

This is an exceptional opportunity to influence the future of one of the world's leading philanthropic institutions and help steward the people and culture that power its local and global impact.

Key Responsibilities

The Managing Director will lead the Foundation's comprehensive People & Culture function and oversee all major human capital initiatives, including, but not limited to:

Executive Leadership and Strategic Partnership

Serve as a member of the leadership advisory team, contributing to organizational strategy, policy development, and enterprise decision-making.
Advise the President and senior leaders on workforce planning, organizational effectiveness, culture, employee engagement, and organizational change.
Position People & Culture as a proactive and influential strategic partner, ensuring people, organizational, and culture implications are considered early in enterprise decisions and helping leaders anticipate rather than simply respond to workforce needs.

Organizational Effectiveness and Change Management

Help strengthen organizational agility, decision-making, prioritization, and accountability, enabling the Foundation to adapt effectively while preserving its deeply collaborative culture.
Champion the thoughtful use of technology, including emerging AI-enabled tools, to modernize people practices, improve efficiency, reduce unnecessary administrative burden, and enable new and more effective ways of working.
Utilize people analytics and workforce data to inform talent and organizational decisions.
Lead organizational change and transformation efforts, including any organizational redesign and culture change, to support evolving organizational needs and strategic priorities.

Employee Engagement, Team Building, and Culture

Lead initiatives that strengthen staff engagement, connection, collaboration, team building, and employee recognition across the Foundation.
Strengthen and sustain an inclusive workplace culture aligned with the Foundation’s mission and values in partnership with the Equity Office and the Just Imperative, where all employees feel valued and supported to do their best work.
Foster a culture that combines trust, care, and inclusion with clear expectations, candid feedback, accountability, continuous learning, innovation, and a shared commitment to high performance.

Employee Relations and Policy Administration

Lead employee relations and serve as a trusted advisor on complex workplace matters, including conflict resolution, mediation, and sensitive organizational challenges.
Oversee the development, implementation, and administration of HR policies and procedures.
Working with the Office of the General Counsel to ensure compliance with applicable employment laws and best practices.

Talent Acquisition, Onboarding, and Workforce Planning

Develop workforce planning strategies that align talent needs with organizational priorities.
Oversee talent acquisition strategies and processes to attract exceptional and mission-aligned talent and ensure recruitment practices support the Foundation's commitment to excellence and broad perspectives.
Oversee onboarding and orientation programs that successfully integrate new employees into the Foundation's culture and operations.

Performance Management and Succession Planning

Oversee the Foundation's performance management systems and processes.
Strengthen managers and equip leaders to set clear expectations, support employee growth, provide meaningful feedback, navigate difficult conversations, differentiate performance, and hold people accountable with fairness and consistency.
Lead enterprise-wide succession planning efforts to ensure leadership continuity and long-term organizational resilience.

Learning, Development, and Leadership Growth

Conduct and oversee organizational and individual needs assessments to identify development opportunities and strengthen organizational capabilities.
Direct and develop approaches to adult learning and professional growth that support employee development and career advancement for emerging, mid-level, and senior leaders.

Total Rewards

Lead the Foundation's total rewards strategy, including benefits and total compensation.
Ensure compensation and benefits programs remain competitive, equitable, and aligned with organizational goals and talent needs.
Monitor market trends and recommend enhancements that support attraction, retention, and employee well-being.

Internal Communications and Special Initiatives

Oversee internal communications related to people and culture, and partner with leadership ensuring communication is clear, timely, and transparent and help employees understand what is changing, why, and what it means for them.
Lead and execute cross-functional special initiatives that advance strategic workforce, culture, and organizational objectives.

Governance and Enterprise Leadership

Serve as a member of the Foundation's Crisis Management Team.
Partner with the President and senior leadership to support the Board on People & Culture matters, providing relevant insights, analysis, and recommendations on executive talent, succession, compensation, workforce risk, and other people-related priorities as appropriate.

The Candidate

Experience

15+ years of progressive human resources leadership experience, including significant experience in senior enterprise-level roles; prior experience in the non-profit or philanthropic sector is a plus.
Broad-based expertise across the people agenda, including talent and leadership development, organizational effectiveness, workforce planning, performance management, total rewards, employee relations, talent acquisition, and HR operations and technology.

The Associate Director of Advancement is a frontline fundraiser responsible for generating philanthropic revenue by managing a portfolio of approximately 100–125 major-gift donors and prospects. POSITION SUMMARY

The Chief Operating Officer owns the full delivery-and-operations engine of the company across the entire asset lifecycle — from contracted project through engineering handoff, construction, commissioning, and long-term operation of biosolids thermal drying and gasification facilities.
Because Stircor designs, builds, owns, and operates its assets under long-term take-or-pay service agreements, the COO is ultimately accountable for whether each site delivers against its contractual performance obligations: throughput, uptime, output specifications, and environmental compliance. This is the executive who converts signed contracts into reliably operating plants and keeps them performing over a 15-to-20-year horizon.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Project Delivery

–   Own the path from engineering handoff through construction and commissioning for new and expanding sites, on schedule and on budget.
–   Partner closely with Engineering (design intent, operability, constructability) and the Head of Construction (site execution) to ensure the plant that gets built is the plant that can meet its contracted numbers.
–   Establish stage-gate discipline across design, build, and startup so operational readiness is proven before revenue obligations begin.
Operations & Maintenance

–   Run the drying and gasification systems day to day across all operating sites with consistent standards.
–   Standardize SOPs, preventive maintenance programs, spare-parts strategy, and equipment reliability practices across the portfolio.
–   Ensure operational discipline that preserves equipment warranties, including warranty terms conditioned on Stircor-employee operation.
–   Build operator staffing, training, and certification programs that scale as the portfolio grows.
Performance & Contract Compliance

–   Hold accountability for each site’s performance against its take-or-pay obligations, minimizing penalty exposure and protecting the municipal relationship.
–   Establish operational KPIs and reporting that give leadership and the board a clear, real-time read on how each site is tracking.
Safety, Environmental & Regulatory

–   Own EHS across all facilities — worker safety around thermal equipment, air-permit and emissions compliance, EPA biosolids and PFAS-related requirements.
–   Maintain licenses, permits, and regulatory standing in good order at every site.
Multi-Site & Multi-Entity Management

–   Manage a geographically distributed operation spanning the company’s operating entities (SSoFL, SSoGA, SSoTN) with uniform standards and clear site-level accountability.
–   Turn what works at one site into a repeatable operating playbook that supports scaling into new contracts.
Customer / Utility Relationships

–   Serve as senior operational point of contact for municipal wastewater clients, where consistent delivery is what earns renewals, referrals, and the next award.

QUALIFICATIONS

–   15+ years in operations leadership within process-intensive infrastructure — thermal processing, energy/power, water/wastewater, chemical, or heavy industrial (build-own-operate or EPC experience strongly preferred).
–   Demonstrated ownership of both capital project delivery and long-run O&M of operating assets.
–   Deep EHS and environmental-compliance fluency in a permitted, regulated operating environment.
–   Track record standardizing operations across multiple sites and scaling an operating organization.
–   Strong commercial literacy — able to manage to contract terms, performance guarantees, and budget.
–   Engineering or technical degree preferred; operations, safety, or MBA credentials a plus.

SUCCESS IN THE FIRST 12–18 MONTHS

–   All operating sites metering to contract, with a clear performance-reporting cadence in place.
–   A standardized, portfolio-wide O&M and SOP framework that new sites can adopt on day one.
–   Clean EHS and regulatory standing across the footprint.
–   New-site delivery de-risked through disciplined engineering-to-commissioning handoffs.

new_jobs.title: Deputy Director, Thurgood Marshall Institute
new_jobs.description:
The NAACP Legal Defense & Educational Fund, Inc. (LDF) is the country’s first and foremost civil and human rights law organization. Founded in 1940 under the leadership of Thurgood Marshall, who subsequently became the first Black U.S. Supreme Court Justice, LDF was launched at a time when the nation’s aspirations for equality and due process of law were stifled by widespread state-sponsored racial inequality. From that era to the present, LDF’s mission has been transformative — to achieve racial justice, equality, and an inclusive society.

LDF’s litigation, public policy advocacy, and public education programs in the substantive areas of criminal justice, economic justice, education, and political participation seek to ensure the fundamental and basic human rights of all people to quality education, economic opportunity, the right to vote and fully participate in democracy, and the right to a fair and just judicial system. LDF continues to make an impact in the area of public service and was recognized by Fast Company as one of its 2023 Brands That Matter under its public service category.

The Thurgood Marshall Institute

Since its founding under the leadership of Thurgood Marshall in 1940, LDF has been committed to transforming this nation’s promise of equality into reality for all Americans. In 2015, LDF celebrated its 75th anniversary with the launch of the Thurgood Marshall Institute (TMI). The Institute is a collaborative research and archival hub within LDF that combines a multidisciplinary approach to advocacy with LDF’s traditional litigation strengths to advance a modern vision of racial justice. The Institute’s goals are to enhance LDF’s use and mobilization of research, archives, and public education to increase its capacity to fight for racial equity, justice, and a more inclusive democracy through targeted advocacy and high-impact communications campaigns.

Through TMI, LDF generates and integrates innovative research, advocacy, archival materials, and strategic communications aimed at educating the public and key decision-makers. This added capacity leverages LDF’s litigation expertise, advocacy experience, and unique leadership role on matters of race, law, and policy to shape the narrative on racial justice and equity. Through targeted campaigns that attack entrenched problems of racial bias, TMI advances holistic strategies to achieve obtainable and lasting solutions on issues of criminal justice, political participation, education, and economic opportunity. In addition, the Institute serves as an active convener of thought-leaders from various disciplines to engage on cutting-edge issues of racial justice in both public and private fora.

In 2024, TMI launched LDF Recollection: A Civil Rights Legal Archive . The website contains stories and primary source materials documenting the history of LDF and the Civil Rights Movement in the U.S. This initiative represents a significant milestone in LDF’s mission to preserve and promote our legacy of civil rights, activism, and advocacy. The core of the website is a searchable digital collection with over 12,000 legal documents, letters, photographs, press releases, original oral history interviews, and other materials from the LDF Archives. The archivists’ work is ongoing as they actively survey, arrange, describe, and digitize select records from LDF’s collection of over 8,000 boxes and multiple terabytes of born-digital records. Their workflow also includes a final step in which the team’s Archives Counsel reviews digitized documents to ensure they do not contain privileged, confidential, or sensitive information.

LDF operates in a hybrid work environment where employees are expected to be in the office a minimum of two days per week, unless otherwise indicated.

Along with a resume and cover letter, applicants are expected to submit an independently authored piece of writing. While it may have undergone review or editing by others, it should primarily reflect your own work.

Responsibilities

Departmental Leadership

Reports directly to the TMI Director and provides supervision across both the Research and Archives teams.
Serve as a thought-partner with the TMI Director to develop and implement strategic goals for the department, ensuring alignment with broader organizational objectives.
Lead department meetings and retreats, including agenda development in collaboration with the TMI Director and Managers, to ensure strategic alignment and team engagement.
Collaborate with TMI Director on budgeting and the recruitment and hiring of key Research and Archives staff, including TMI fellows and scholars, to ensure alignment with organizational and departmental needs and strategic priorities.
Guide and mentor staff to fully understand and effectively execute their job responsibilities, fostering accountability through performance reviews, professional development, and leadership opportunities.
Build and maintain relationships with internal and external stakeholders to enhance departmental initiatives and resources, which include managing budgets, grant compliance, and vendor contracts in coordination with the TMI Director.
Develop and complete annual professional development plans to stay current on developments in the field.
Represents TMI in public forums, including conferences, media appearances, and other external engagements, to elevate the Institute’s research, archival projects, and advocacy.
Help identify and support cross-functional projects that connect research, archives, and public education.

Archives Oversight

Lead in coordination with the TMI Director the strategy, development, and execution of archival projects to preserve and promote LDF’s civil rights legacy in collaboration with the team.
Work with the Archives Department on refinement, implementation, and management of LDF’s efforts to review its archived records for publication.
Work with the Archives Department on the dissemination and promotion of LDF’s archival records, including those housed at the Library of Congress, both internally and externally.
Support archives team members through meetings to ensure work product meets high-quality standards, maintains TMI’s voice, and advances LDF advocacy goals within an established timeframe and budget.

Research Oversight

Develop and support the implementation of the research agenda to align with TMI and LDF’s strategic priorities, including qualitative and quantitative research design, public-facing reports, and policy briefs in collaboration with TMI Director.
Supervise research team members, including senior researchers, fellows, and associated team members, to ensure products meet high-quality research standards, maintain TMI’s voice, advance LDF advocacy goals, and are completed within an established timeframe and budget.
Support TMI researchers in the preparation and submission of IRB applications, grant submissions, and the submission of grant reports of research activities.
Review research findings for publication, ensuring that reports, papers, and presentations accurately reflect the data and adhere to ethical standards across all research stages, from proposal to publication, to prevent misconduct and promote transparency.
Coordinate the evaluation of TMI’s publications for external review in collaboration with the TMI Director to ensure the integrity and quality of research outputs. Selecting appropriate reviewers, facilitating constructive dialogue, and synthesizing insights guide revisions or project advancements, maintaining scholarly excellence and innovation.
Supervise the oversight of the Social Science Research Network (SSRN), National Police Funding Database, and the Death Row USA Report, ensuring the reports and website data are current.
Develop and update research policies and procedures (manual).
Oversee interdepartmental rapid research requests, ensuring that requests are aligned with LDF’s strategic priorities.
Provide editorial oversight and strategic review of TMI’s research publications to ensure rigor, clarity, and alignment with LDF’s advocacy goals.
Facilitate interdisciplinary collaborations with scholars and advocacy partners.

Qualifications

Minimum of 10 years of professional experience with expertise in civil rights history, academic research, or civil rights advocacy, including supervisory experience.

Experience developing and managing publications, research workflows, and strategic campaigns required.

Preferred

Experience managing budgets.
Successful record of using multiple campaign strategies to achieve positive social change, including, for example, advocacy, research, archives, organizing, communications, and litigation.
Familiarity with open-access publication platforms, data visualization tools, or digital humanities methods is a plus.

The Foundation

The John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation
is one of the nation's largest independent philanthropic foundations, dedicated to building a more just, verdant, and peaceful world. Established in 1978 through the legacy of John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur, the Foundation supports creative people, effective institutions, and influential networks that are advancing solutions to some of the world's most pressing social and environmental challenges.

Through programmatic grantmaking, impact investing, strategic partnerships, convening power, and collaborations at scale, MacArthur strives toward transformative change on some of the world’s most pressing social issues, including the existential threats of climate change
, criminal justice reform
, revitalizing local news
in the United States, expanding who creates, uses, and benefits from artificial intelligence
, strengthening Native communities
, and empowering young people in Nigeria
.

In addition to their award programs, MacArthur Fellows
, and 100&Change
, the Foundation continues its historic commitments to the role of journalism
in a responsible and responsive democracy and to the strength and vitality of their headquarters city, Chicago
. The Foundation also works to strengthen ecosystems of people, organizations and networks working on deploying catalytic capital
,
strengthening the philanthropic sector
and addressing the social impacts of technology
.

Across its portfolio, the Foundation approaches its work with urgency, intellectual rigor, adaptability, and a commitment to continuous learning, leveraging grants, impact investments, communications, convenings, contracts, and partnerships to achieve measurable and lasting impact.

Since its founding, MacArthur has awarded more than $9.19 billion through grants and impact investments
to approximately 11,000 organizations and individuals and has supported work in 119 countries. Headquartered in Chicago, the Foundation maintains offices in India and Nigeria. As of December 31, 2025, MacArthur's assets totaled approximately $9.9 billion. In 2025 alone, the Foundation provided approximately $561.6 million in grants and program-related investments and committed an estimated $647 million in charitable spending, reflecting its continued commitment to investing boldly in solutions that create meaningful and enduring change.

The Opportunity

The MacArthur Foundation seeks an accomplished, strategic, and values-driven executive to serve as its next Managing Director, People & Culture. Reporting directly to the Foundation’s President and serving as a member of the Foundation's executive leadership team, the Managing Director will provide vision, strategy, and leadership for all aspects of the Foundation's people and culture agenda. MacArthur is navigating a period of change and heightened ambition. As the Foundation responds to an increasingly complex external environment, embraces new technologies, and seeks to deliver greater impact without proportionate growth in its workforce, the Managing Director will help shape how the organization works, leads, collaborates, and adapts. This leader will help MacArthur sustain the best of its highly collaborative, intellectually curious, and mission-driven culture while strengthening organizational agility, accountability, clarity, and effectiveness.

This is an exceptional opportunity to influence the future of one of the world's leading philanthropic institutions and help steward the people and culture that power its local and global impact.

Key Responsibilities

The Managing Director will lead the Foundation's comprehensive People & Culture function and oversee all major human capital initiatives, including, but not limited to:

Executive Leadership and Strategic Partnership

Serve as a member of the leadership advisory team, contributing to organizational strategy, policy development, and enterprise decision-making.
Advise the President and senior leaders on workforce planning, organizational effectiveness, culture, employee engagement, and organizational change.
Position People & Culture as a proactive and influential strategic partner, ensuring people, organizational, and culture implications are considered early in enterprise decisions and helping leaders anticipate rather than simply respond to workforce needs.

Organizational Effectiveness and Change Management

Help strengthen organizational agility, decision-making, prioritization, and accountability, enabling the Foundation to adapt effectively while preserving its deeply collaborative culture.
Champion the thoughtful use of technology, including emerging AI-enabled tools, to modernize people practices, improve efficiency, reduce unnecessary administrative burden, and enable new and more effective ways of working.
Utilize people analytics and workforce data to inform talent and organizational decisions.
Lead organizational change and transformation efforts, including any organizational redesign and culture change, to support evolving organizational needs and strategic priorities.

Employee Engagement, Team Building, and Culture

Lead initiatives that strengthen staff engagement, connection, collaboration, team building, and employee recognition across the Foundation.
Strengthen and sustain an inclusive workplace culture aligned with the Foundation’s mission and values in partnership with the Equity Office and the Just Imperative, where all employees feel valued and supported to do their best work.
Foster a culture that combines trust, care, and inclusion with clear expectations, candid feedback, accountability, continuous learning, innovation, and a shared commitment to high performance.

Employee Relations and Policy Administration

Lead employee relations and serve as a trusted advisor on complex workplace matters, including conflict resolution, mediation, and sensitive organizational challenges.
Oversee the development, implementation, and administration of HR policies and procedures.
Working with the Office of the General Counsel to ensure compliance with applicable employment laws and best practices.

Develop workforce planning strategies that align talent needs with organizational priorities.
Oversee talent acquisition strategies and processes to attract exceptional and mission-aligned talent and ensure recruitment practices support the Foundation's commitment to excellence and broad perspectives.
Oversee onboarding and orientation programs that successfully integrate new employees into the Foundation's culture and operations.

Performance Management and Succession Planning

Oversee the Foundation's performance management systems and processes.
Strengthen managers and equip leaders to set clear expectations, support employee growth, provide meaningful feedback, navigate difficult conversations, differentiate performance, and hold people accountable with fairness and consistency.
Lead enterprise-wide succession planning efforts to ensure leadership continuity and long-term organizational resilience.

Learning, Development, and Leadership Growth

Total Rewards

Monitor market trends and recommend enhancements that support attraction, retention, and employee well-being.

Internal Communications and Special Initiatives

Lead and execute cross-functional special initiatives that advance strategic workforce, culture, and organizational objectives.

Governance and Enterprise Leadership

POSITION SUMMARY

The Chief Operating Officer owns the full delivery-and-operations engine of the company across the entire asset lifecycle — from contracted project through engineering handoff, construction, commissioning, and long-term operation of biosolids thermal drying and gasification facilities.
Because Stircor designs, builds, owns, and operates its assets under long-term take-or-pay service agreements, the COO is ultimately accountable for whether each site delivers against its contractual performance obligations: throughput, uptime, output specifications, and environmental compliance. This is the executive who converts signed contracts into reliably operating plants and keeps them performing over a 15-to-20-year horizon.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Project Delivery

–   Own the path from engineering handoff through construction and commissioning for new and expanding sites, on schedule and on budget.
–   Partner closely with Engineering (design intent, operability, constructability) and the Head of Construction (site execution) to ensure the plant that gets built is the plant that can meet its contracted numbers.
–   Establish stage-gate discipline across design, build, and startup so operational readiness is proven before revenue obligations begin.
Operations & Maintenance

–   Run the drying and gasification systems day to day across all operating sites with consistent standards.
–   Standardize SOPs, preventive maintenance programs, spare-parts strategy, and equipment reliability practices across the portfolio.
–   Ensure operational discipline that preserves equipment warranties, including warranty terms conditioned on Stircor-employee operation.
–   Build operator staffing, training, and certification programs that scale as the portfolio grows.
Performance & Contract Compliance

–   Hold accountability for each site’s performance against its take-or-pay obligations, minimizing penalty exposure and protecting the municipal relationship.
–   Establish operational KPIs and reporting that give leadership and the board a clear, real-time read on how each site is tracking.
Safety, Environmental & Regulatory

–   Own EHS across all facilities — worker safety around thermal equipment, air-permit and emissions compliance, EPA biosolids and PFAS-related requirements.
–   Maintain licenses, permits, and regulatory standing in good order at every site.
Multi-Site & Multi-Entity Management

–   Manage a geographically distributed operation spanning the company’s operating entities (SSoFL, SSoGA, SSoTN) with uniform standards and clear site-level accountability.
–   Turn what works at one site into a repeatable operating playbook that supports scaling into new contracts.
Customer / Utility Relationships

–   Serve as senior operational point of contact for municipal wastewater clients, where consistent delivery is what earns renewals, referrals, and the next award.

QUALIFICATIONS

–   15+ years in operations leadership within process-intensive infrastructure — thermal processing, energy/power, water/wastewater, chemical, or heavy industrial (build-own-operate or EPC experience strongly preferred).
–   Demonstrated ownership of both capital project delivery and long-run O&M of operating assets.
–   Deep EHS and environmental-compliance fluency in a permitted, regulated operating environment.
–   Track record standardizing operations across multiple sites and scaling an operating organization.
–   Strong commercial literacy — able to manage to contract terms, performance guarantees, and budget.
–   Engineering or technical degree preferred; operations, safety, or MBA credentials a plus.

SUCCESS IN THE FIRST 12–18 MONTHS

–   All operating sites metering to contract, with a clear performance-reporting cadence in place.
–   A standardized, portfolio-wide O&M and SOP framework that new sites can adopt on day one.
–   Clean EHS and regulatory standing across the footprint.
–   New-site delivery de-risked through disciplined engineering-to-commissioning handoffs.
